correctness.rationale: All open edge-neighbourhoods reduce to three necessary-and-sufficient colour multiplicity conditions over nine ordered page types. Clipping each type count at three preserves equality to one even after deletion of the edge colour, since the only negative correction is minus one. An exact finite check of all 4^9=262144 reduced vectors proves the 18-family classification whenever n>=5; it excludes other vectors of total at least five. The labelled count is 3*(6*n+12*n*(n-1)). Direct graph-edge exhaustive 3-colour checks give 198 at n=3, 1080 at n=4 and 810 at n=5, agreeing with an independent orbit enumerator. A separate general two-colour contradiction establishes chromatic index three, and an explicit 3-colour construction supplies the upper bound. Standalone Python verification has been rerun from the provided path; no infinity argument is extrapolated from bounded n.

value.rationale: This provides a complete exact counting invariant for a natural infinite common-edge triangle family under a recently developed colouring model, rather than another loose existence bound. A 3-colour palette admits exponentially many raw assignments but only 18*n*(2*n-1) feasible assignments for n>=5; all permitted colourings have one or two exceptional pages. The rigid family classification, n=3 and n=4 exceptions, and polynomial-versus-exponential gap give motivated structure and a reusable benchmark for open-neighbourhood edge-colouring methods.
